Motorcycle Insurance Types Explained

UK law requires at minimum Third Party Only insurance, but understanding all three levels helps you choose the right cover.

Third Party Only (TPO)

Cheapest option. Covers damage to other people and property only. Does not cover your bike, theft, or fire. Best for old or cheap bikes.

Third Party Fire & Theft (TPFT)

Mid-range. Adds theft and fire cover to TPO. Still does not cover accidental damage to your bike.

Comprehensive

Full protection including accidental damage, vandalism, and personal injury. Best for new, expensive, or financed bikes. Read our Motorcycle Helmet Safety Ratings Explained guide for more. Note: Comprehensive is sometimes cheaper than TPFT due to how insurers price risk. Always compare quotes for all three levels.
keyTakeaways: UK law requires at least Third Party Only insurance to ride on the road.
TPO covers damage to other people and property but not your own bike, theft or fire.
TPFT adds theft and fire cover but still excludes accidental damage to your bike.
Comprehensive gives the fullest protection, including accidental damage and personal injury.
Comprehensive can sometimes be cheaper than TPFT, so always compare all three levels.

faq.q: What is the minimum motorcycle insurance required by UK law?
faq.a: UK law requires at least Third Party Only (TPO) cover to ride on public roads. TPO pays for injury to other people and damage to their property if you are at fault, but it does not cover your own bike, or loss from theft or fire. It is the legal minimum, not necessarily the best value.

faq.q: What is the difference between TPFT and comprehensive?
faq.a: Third Party Fire & Theft (TPFT) adds cover for your bike being stolen or damaged by fire to the basic third-party protection, but it still will not pay for accidental damage to your own machine. Comprehensive goes further, covering accidental damage, vandalism and often personal injury, making it the fullest level of protection available.

faq.q: Is comprehensive insurance always the most expensive?
faq.a: Surprisingly not. Comprehensive cover is sometimes cheaper than TPFT, because insurers associate riders who choose comprehensive with lower overall risk and price accordingly. This is why you should always get quotes for all three levels rather than assuming the basic option is cheapest. Compare like-for-like before deciding.

faq.q: Which insurance level should I choose for my bike?
faq.a: Match the cover to the bike's value and your circumstances. TPO can make sense for an old, low-value bike, TPFT suits a mid-value machine where theft is a concern, and comprehensive is best for new, expensive or financed bikes where accidental damage cover matters. Always compare quotes, as pricing does not always follow this logic.

faq.q: Does insurance cover me riding other bikes?
faq.a: Not automatically. Some comprehensive policies historically included limited third-party cover to ride other people's bikes, but this is increasingly rare and often restricted. Never assume you are covered; check your policy documents or ask your insurer directly. Riding uninsured, even briefly, is a serious offence with heavy penalties.
